definitions.gloss: Ihara Saikaku; Edo-period novelist and poet
definitions.explanation: An Osaka writer and haikai poet of the Genroku era, the founder of ukiyo-zōshi, popular fiction about the loves and money worries of townspeople.

examples.english: Ihara Saikaku's novels vividly portray people swept along by money and love.

notes:
USAGE:
Often called simply {西鶴|さいかく}. His books are the first {浮世草子|うきよぞうし} ("books of the floating world").

CULTURAL NOTE:
With the haiku poet Bashō and the playwright Chikamatsu Monzaemon, Saikaku is one of the three great writers of the Genroku era (around 1700). Japanese school literature courses teach him as the writer of the merchant class.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {好色一代男|こうしょくいちだいおとこ}: The Life of an Amorous Man (1682), his first novel
- {日本永代蔵|にっぽんえいたいぐら}: The Japanese Family Storehouse, stories of making and losing fortunes
- {世間胸算用|せけんむねさんよう}: stories of townspeople struggling to settle their debts on New Year's Eve
